summary: GPT-5.5 is OpenAI's dedicated system card for a reasoning model aimed at complex coding, research, and tool-mediated work. The card reports High biological/chemical and High-but-not-Critical cybersecurity Preparedness treatment, expanded cyber safeguards, improved agentic workspace handling, and residual issues in monitorability, prompt injection, factuality, and low-severity misalignment.

capabilities.text: OpenAI describes GPT-5.5 as a model for complex real-world work across coding, research, analysis, documents, spreadsheets, and tools.
Agentic workspace evaluations show improved destructive-action avoidance, perfect reversion, and preservation of user work compared with earlier models.
HealthBench scores improve over GPT-5.4 Thinking on the standard, Hard, and Professional variants while Consensus is roughly flat.
Cyber testing shows strong performance in end-to-end ranges and third-party narrow cyber tasks, supporting a High cyber capability classification.
AI self-improvement results remain below High even though GPT-5.5 leads compared models on OpenAI's internal research-debugging benchmark.

safety_findings.text: OpenAI classifies GPT-5.5 as High for biological and chemical capability, High but below Critical for cybersecurity, and below High for AI self-improvement.
GPT-5.5 improves agentic workspace safety, especially avoiding destructive changes and preserving user work during long rollouts.
The internal coding-traffic resampling found no severity-4 misalignment and a 0.01% severity-3 rate, while low-severity misalignment increased in some categories.
CoT monitorability remains high overall, but OpenAI reports health-query regressions from monitor false positives and lower agent faithfulness.
External bio testing found strong scientific reasoning but kept sophisticated expert planning and jailbreak uncertainty as biosecurity considerations.
Cyber safeguards were expanded for scaled vulnerability research and exploit chaining, using model training, monitoring, account-level enforcement, and trusted access.
UK AISI found a universal jailbreak against an evaluated cyber-safeguard configuration; OpenAI reports subsequent fixes but not independent final verification by UK AISI.

limitations.text: Many results are offline evaluations and may not reflect full production behavior or the separate GPT-5.5 Pro setting.
The representative-prompt prevalence pipeline is experimental and subject to traffic drift, reconstruction bias, and missing safety-stack layers.
OpenAI says the challenging disallowed-content benchmark consists of hard cases and is not representative of average production traffic.
The internal coding-traffic resampling depends on a simulator and is better treated as a relative deployment-risk signal than an external safety rate.
Preparedness testing is a lower bound because stronger scaffolds, longer rollouts, fine-tuning, or different prompts might elicit more capability.
SecureBio tested pre-release checkpoints and did not systematically evaluate robustness against highly motivated jailbreak attempts.
UK AISI's cyber ranges omit common real-world defensive tooling, and its final safeguard retest did not verify OpenAI's launch configuration.

practical_implications.text: Use GPT-5.5 for complex debugging, multi-step edits, and tool-heavy development where persistence and workspace recovery are valuable.
Keep file-changing sessions reviewable with diffs, tests, and clear ownership boundaries because destructive-action avoidance is not perfect.
Treat tool and connector outputs as untrusted; prompt-injection robustness is strong but leaves residual risk.
Keep cyber tasks authorized and defensive, with narrow scopes and explicit approvals for any exploit-like workflow.
Verify factual claims and research summaries independently because hallucination rates improve but do not disappear.
Use explicit task constraints and checkpoints in long Copilot sessions to reduce over-eager action and low-severity misalignment patterns.

coverage_notes: This digest covers the complete 46-page GPT-5.5 system card, including capabilities, safety, health, hallucination, alignment, bias, Preparedness, external evaluation, and safeguard sections. It treats GPT-5.5 Pro only as the card does: generally proxied by GPT-5.5 results except where the card separately discusses Pro.
